title: Amazon Purchase Predictor Regression Model
text:
Introduction
The Amazon Purchase Predictor Regression Model analyzes purchasing behaviors based on demographic and transaction data. The primary goal was to predict log_total, the total spending amount in log scale, using explanatory variables from the dataset. By implementing regression techniques, this study identifies key factors influencing customer spending habits and provides insight into consumer behavior.

title: Amazon Purchase Predictor Regression Model
text:
Process

Data Preprocessing:

Cleaned and handled missing values.
Normalized and transformed variables where necessary.
Selected relevant features based on correlation and importance.

Model Selection and Training:

Experimented with linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, random forest, and KNN regression.
Tuned hyperparameters using cross-validation for optimal performance.

Feature Engineering:

Identified key explanatory variables such as count_hh4 and count_G, which showed strong correlation with log_total.
Considered interactions between income level and purchasing frequency to refine the model.

title: Amazon Purchase Predictor Regression Model
text:
Outcome
The final model selected was a Random Forest regression model, which achieved:

Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE): 0.1128934
Standard Error (SE): 0.003002182
R-squared Score: Higher than 0.9587, indicating strong predictive power.
Household size, order count, and income level were significant predictors of Amazon purchases.
KNN regression was tested but did not outperform tree-based models in terms of accuracy.

title: LA Airbnb Analysis
text:
Introduction
The LA Airbnb Analysis project analyzes Airbnb listings and reviews in Los Angeles. The objective is to provide insights and strategies that help hosts improve performance and profitability. The project uses listings and review datasets, then focuses on factors that contribute to superhost status, pricing, sentiment, and listing visibility.

title: LA Airbnb Analysis
text:
Process

Host Analysis:

Analyzed key predictors such as response rates, acceptance rates, ratings, profile pictures, and duration of hosting.
Used logistic regression and random forest models to determine factors contributing to superhost status.

Listing Analysis with NLP:

Applied natural language processing to conduct sentiment analysis of reviews.
Used Latent Dirichlet Allocation for topic modeling to identify themes in guest reviews.

Dashboard Development:

Created an interactive dashboard displaying price, room type, beds, ratings, and location.
Included filters for guests to find listings based on their preferences.

Outcome

Key predictors for achieving superhost status included high ratings, acceptance rates, and response rates.
Test accuracies for logistic regression and random forest models were 74% and 76%, respectively.
Suggested strategies included maintaining high ratings, addressing negative reviews, and improving acceptance rates.
Sentiment analysis helped identify common issues with low-rated listings.

text: Java PostgreSQL JDBC

title: To-Do List
text:
Introduction
The To-Do List Application is a Java-based program that allows users to manage tasks with basic CRUD functionality. It uses PostgreSQL as the backend database for task storage and provides an interactive console interface for managing tasks efficiently.

title: To-Do List
text:
Process

Database Setup:

Designed a PostgreSQL database schema with a tasks table.
Defined columns for task ID, name, description, due date, and status.

JDBC Integration:

Established a JDBC connection to interact with the PostgreSQL database.
Implemented SQL queries for inserting, retrieving, updating, and deleting tasks.

Backend Development:

Created a Java application with CRUD operations.
Used prepared statements to prevent SQL injection.

User Interface Implementation:

Developed a console-based UI for task management.
Provided prompts for adding, viewing, updating, and deleting tasks.

title: To-Do List
text:
Features

Add Task: Create a new task with a name, description, due date, and status.
View Tasks: Retrieve and display all tasks stored in the database.
Update Task: Modify the task name and status.
Delete Task: Remove a task from the database permanently.

title: To-Do List
text:
Outcome
The project successfully implements a task management system with fundamental database operations. Future enhancements may include user authentication, task filtering, sorting, and a front-end interface.

title: Diabetes Risk Predictive Modeling
text:
Introduction
This project identifies key factors influencing diabetes diagnosis by analyzing a dataset of 9,538 medical records. The study focuses on the relationships between BMI, HbA1c, family history, and age in predicting diabetes risk. Through statistical modeling and feature selection, the goal was to develop an effective predictive model for diabetes classification.

title: Diabetes Risk Predictive Modeling
text:
Process

Data Preprocessing:

Used a secondary dataset containing demographic, lifestyle, and biometric health data.
Verified that the dataset required minimal cleaning, with no missing values or outliers to remove.
Checked multicollinearity using Variance Inflation Factor, then removed glucose because of strong correlation with HbA1c.

Feature Selection:

Used stepwise regression to identify significant predictors.
Selected age, BMI, HbA1c, and family history for the final model.
Used ANOVA to confirm that the reduced model performed comparably to the full model.

Modeling and Evaluation:

Implemented logistic regression as the primary predictive model.
Performed a 70/30 train-test split and evaluated the model with a confusion matrix, achieving 97% accuracy.
Conducted 5-fold cross-validation with RMSE of 0.146, R-squared of 0.906, and MAE of 0.04.
Plotted the ROC curve, yielding an AUC of 0.99.

Further Exploration:

Explored family history and diabetes risk across age groups.
Analyzed BMI and HbA1c interactions to understand how metabolic indicators correspond with diagnosis likelihood.

title: Diabetes Risk Predictive Modeling
text:
Outcome

Developed a highly accurate logistic regression model for diabetes prediction.
Identified BMI, HbA1c, and age as primary predictors, with family history as a potential modifier.
Demonstrated that early monitoring of metabolic health is important in diabetes prevention.

title: Diabetes Risk Predictive Modeling
text:
Limitations and Future Improvements

The dataset lacked variables such as diet, exercise, and socioeconomic status.
Medical recording variability could introduce measurement inconsistencies.
Future research could investigate gender-specific diabetes risks, BMI and gender interactions, and additional lifestyle or clinical variables.
